newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Coffee seen in range, waiting for NY lead.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Coffee seen in range, waiting for NY lead.

text.p: JULY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
LIFFE coffee futures were expected to trade in a broad range in the near term until New York futures made a decisive move in either direction.
July coffee was called to open about $30 higher after closing $8 up at $1,669 per tonne. July failed to sustain gains above stiff resistance at $1,700 on Monday.

"In the near term, I expect a broad trading range," said Sucden analyst Adrian Haylor. The top of July's range was marked by a chart gap between Monday's high of $1,705 and the March 12 low of $1,730.
Strong support rested near $1,600, a level amid an area where several moving averages and trendlines meet.
The 40-day moving average was at $1,638, the 20-day moving average stood at $1,611 and an uptrend from January lows emerged near $1,577, Haylor said.

But Haylor did not see enough momentum for robusta futures alone to make a decisive break in either direction. He said New York would probably have to be the impetus to prod London markets out of their trading range.
New York's futures had a volatile session on Monday, with July finally ending down 0.10 cent per pound at 194.05 cents after scoring a contract high at 199.

Despite the whipsaw session, analysts in New York remained optimistic on the market though they noted crucial July resistances there above the market at 220 and 224 cents. Support was seen at 187.40 cents.
